title: TABLE OF 76 'CAUSES, BASES, and SOURCES OF ILLUSIONS'

lists.name: 76 causes, bases, and sources of illusions
lists.of: cause, basis, or source of illusions
items: Camouflage, hiding, or 'environmental mimicry or assimilation'.
Deficiencies of fundamental knowledge (e.g., imprecise or undefined [mathematics, geometry, physics, ethics, etc]).
Erroneous substitution of part for whole.
Excessive abstraction, theoretical fictions, or neglect of concrete facts.

Fallacious equation of [parvitude, rarity, singularity, etc] with insignificance [e.g., discounting of what is small, exaggeration of the importance of what is large; erroneous proportionation of size to importance].
Hierarchy (multiplicity of confusing and interfering levels).

Ignorance about illusion in general (its [diversity, categories, taxa, omnipresence, signs, causes, genesis, laws, instances and spectrum of exemplifications, transformations, transcendences, degrees, related phenomena, powers, etc]).
Imperfections or costs of common sense.
Information overload, mental or perceptual fatigue, or 'environmental burial'.
Lack of a transcendent (to suggest [imperfection, finitude, etc]) or a companion.
Lack of self-criticism, self-ignorance, or lack of criticism in general.
Logical fallacies or misapplication of general principles.
Mass delusion or other related idola.
Misconstrual of function from appearance or mis-supposition of appearance from function.
Monoideism (excessive preoccupation with a single, fixed idea).
Neglect of scientific procedures [testing, experimentation, prediction, validation, reproduction, statistical evaluation, induction, deduction, rich hypothecation, etc].
Neuropsychological heredity (e.g., inherited [modes, gestalten, or elements] of [perception, thought, feeling, or action]).
Neurosis, psychosis, or other forms of irrationality.
Overgeneralization, exaggeration, infinitization, absolutization, non-qualification, eternalization, idealization, etc.
'Pan-Truth' (misapplication of the doctrine so-named) or pan-paradoxy.
Perspective (e.g., [limited, fixed, specialized, or local]); or defective [coordinate systems or coordinates].
Poor or defective correlation of data, or mis-combined sensa or percepts.
Pseudo-averaging (attempted averaging of what cannot be averaged).
'Pseudo-convergences' (e.g., in data series) or regressional fallacies.
Psychophysical boundary values, objective similarity, non-discrimination, under-differentiation, or mis-analogy.
Random patterns, coincidences, juxtapositions, or 'background noise'.
Unconstrained imagination or 'pseudo-perception' (spurious acts of perception that are assumed to have occurred but that in fact did not occur).
Unwillingness to doubt or to consider the possibility of illusion; or complacency.

notes: Handwritten annotations and the smaller reference sheet are not included.
